newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds lose some earlier gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds lose some earlier gains in late trade.

text.p: Irish government bonds lost some of their earlier gains in thin late trade on Tuesday in line with UK gilts which showed losses on Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's budget speech, dealers said.
UK analysts said PSBR forecasts involved tight fiscal policy but they added that the inflation view remained optimistic.
They said a UK rate rise was still seen as likely.
By 1635 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond had risen 40 pence from Monday's close to 102.55 to yield 5.80 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 45 pence at 109.55 to yield 6.53 percent.
Irish dealers said a close eye was being kept on the currency markets as the punt remained at just above parity against sterling. -- Damien Lynch, Dublin newsroom.
